messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: fixing print() & diagnostic_stream in command
parts:
I'm trying to fix the broken print() command so that it
prints every iteration. Stan 2.0.0 broke it.

Should print() print to the diagnostic_stream variable
in gm/command.hpp?

Or should it always print to std::cout?

As is, it's not printing anywhere. There weren't enough
arguments being passed into the writers (the danger
of default values --- I'm thinking we should stop using
these whenerever we can get away with it because they've
caused us no end of trouble like this).

I just changed the command so that print() always
prints to std::cout, but that meant replacing some
uses of diagnostic_stream with &std::cout. And I'm
not sure that's right.

There's a local variable "diagnostic_stream" in
command.hpp that's being set if a diagnostic file
is specified and left as 0 otherwise.

1. print() always prints to std::cout

2. print() prints to the diagnostic stream
if a diagnostic_file is specified in the command

3. both of the above

We could also print to std::cerr, but that's tricky given
that std::cout and std::cerr aren't synched.

Then there's the issue of what to do for optimization.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] fixing print() & diagnostic_stream in command
parts:
I would prefer diagnostic_stream not be muddied up with print
output, as it would make using the diagnostic_stream a pain --
at the moment diagnosic_stream is basically treated like a csv,
or whatever Stan format we define in the future. If you were to
inject the print output it would have to at least be formatted as comments
(right now #, but again we don't really have an output spec) to
avoid breaking the current uses of the stream. Another concern
is the size of the resulting diagnostic_stream which would grow
rapidly.
